title: Bihar
name: Bihar
intro: Bihar lost eighty-one assembly seats in November 2000, when Jharkhand was carved out of its southern districts. The 243 that remained had been drawn by the 1976 order for an undivided Bihar, and they were contested twice in 2005, in February and again in October after a hung assembly, before the 2008 order redrew them. Elections before 2005 were fought on the undivided 324-seat map and are not shown here.

map_caveats: The pre-2008 boundaries have been georectified. The source digitisation of the 1976-order map was displaced relative to the 2008-order map; the correction was fitted on the outer boundary of the state and raises the agreement between the two outlines from an intersection-over-union of 0.96 to 0.98.

Only the two elections of 2005 are shown on the pre-2008 map. Bihar had 324 assembly seats until Jharkhand was separated in November 2000, and the elections of 1980 to 2000 were contested on that larger map, whose constituencies are not the ones shown here.

Territory lineage is given on two footings, and each seat record states which applies to it. For 235 of the 243 pre-2008 seats the link is derived from the text of the 1976 and 2008 orders. For the remainder the successor shown is the one holding the largest share of the old seat's area, inferred from the boundaries alone.
Territory percentages are measured from the mapped boundaries in every case, and are areal shares, not shares of the electorate.
The reservation status of the post-2008 seats is taken from the constituency geometry, the source that carries it for this state.
footnotes: Bihar was divided on 15 November 2000, when Jharkhand was formed from its eighteen southern districts, taking eighty-one of the 324 assembly constituencies drawn by the 1976 order.
Reservation status reflects the category in force at the time of the relevant order, not any later reclassification.
